div.l: Of maystres / had he / moo than thries ten
That were of lawe / expert and curious
Of which ther were / a doseyn in that house
Worthy to have stywardys / of reente and londe
Of any lord / that is in Ingelonde
To make hym lyve / bi his propre good
In honour detteles / but if he were wood
Or lyve as scarsly / as hym lyste desyre
And able for to helpyn / al a shyre
In any caas / that myhte falle or happe
And yet this manciple / set here alder cappe
A ReveTHe reve was slender / a coleryk man
His beerd was shave / as nyh as ever he can
His heris were bi his eris / rownde and shorn
His top was docked / lyk a prest biforn
Wel longe were his leggis / and wel leene
Like a staff / ther was no calf seene
Wel covde he kepe / a gerner and a bynne
Ther was noon auditovr / that covde of hym wynne
Wel woste he bi the drouhte / and bi the reyne
The yeldyng of his seed / and of his greyne
His lordys shepp / his neet his deyrye
His swyn his hors / his stoor and his pultrye
Was holy in this revys governynge
And bi covenaunt / yaf he reknynge
Syn that his lord was twenti wynter of age
Ther covde no man / castyn hym in a rerage
Ther nas baylyff / ne herde / ne other hyne
That he ne knewe his sleyht and his covyne ·
They were a drad of hym / as of the deth
His wonnyng was wol fayre vp on an heth
With grene trees shadwed / was his place
He covde betyr than his lord / purchase
